newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares barely lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares barely lower in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged lower in continued weak trade on Monday as liquidity shortage persisted due to a forthcoming holiday as well as political caution, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed three points, or 0.2 percent lower at 1,502 after drifting in a narrow range between 1,493 and 1,515. It had lost 4.1 percent last week.
Trade volume dropped to 13.13 trillion lira ($99.5 million) from Friday's 14.13 trillion ($107.5 million).
The stock market will be closed from mid-Thursday until April 24 due to a 4-1/2-day religious holiday to between April 17-21, to be followed by an official holiday on April 23.
"Political uncertainty and the National Security Council (MGK) meeting due on April 26 hinder demand," Murat Elbelger from Finans investment said.

Investors switching to cash or repo deals ahead of the holiday caused volume to shrink last week. Several brokers await some buying in the next two days when settlements of transactions will be delayed to after the holiday.
"The index may continue to drift between 1,480 support and 1,530 resistance in the short term. More trade volume is needed for it to exceed this range," Elbelger said.
